key_insight: A Cu2NiGeS4 thin-film solar cell paired with In2S3 and MoTe2 charge-selective layers can be tuned in simulation to deliver very high efficiency by improving carrier separation and reducing recombination.
engineering_relevance: The study provides device-design guidance for optimizing absorber, interface, and transport-layer parameters in earth-abundant thin-film photovoltaics.
method: SCAPS-1D simulation of an In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 heterostructure
Systematic sweep of thickness, doping, defects, recombination, resistance, temperature, and illumination
Band-diagram and carrier-transport analysis to identify limiting loss mechanisms
evidence_signal: The optimized device is reported to reach 28.44% PCE with VOC 0.984 V, JSC 34.39 mA/cm2, and FF 84.04% under AM1.5G at 300 K, exceeding the earlier 6.25–21.17% range cited for CNGS devices.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, so real-device performance may be lower if material quality, interfaces, or fabrication tolerances deviate from the modeled assumptions.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
